gla.label: Assembly constituency
gla.blurb: London Assembly constituencies — each one is a whole group of two to four boroughs.

borough.label: borough
borough.blurb: The 32 London boroughs and the City of London.

pcon.label: constituency
pcon.blurb: UK Parliament constituencies on the 2024 boundaries.

oa.label: output area
oa.blurb: Census output areas of about 330 people.

groups.label: People
groups.blurb: How many, how densely, and how many to a home.

groups.label: Age
groups.blurb: Where London's children, students and pensioners live.

groups.label: Origins
groups.blurb: Ethnic group, birthplace, passports and identity.

groups.label: Religion
groups.blurb: The one voluntary question on the census form.

groups.label: Migration & language
groups.blurb: When people arrived, and what is spoken at home.

groups.label: Health & care
groups.blurb: Self-reported health, disability and unpaid care.

groups.label: Work & study
groups.blurb: Occupation, social class, activity and qualifications.

groups.label: Housing
groups.blurb: Tenure and the kind of building people live in.

measures.label: Population density
measures.note: Residents per hectare of land. Inland water and tidal foreshore are excluded, so riverside areas are not diluted by the Thames. Output areas are drawn to hold about the same number of people, so at this grain density is essentially a read-out of built form.

measures.label: People per household
measures.note: Residents living in households divided by households. Residents of communal establishments are excluded from the numerator, as they have no household to belong to.

measures.label: Living in communal establishments
measures.note: Halls of residence, care homes, barracks, prisons and hotels. A handful of output areas are almost entirely communal.

measures.label: Median age
measures.note: Interpolated within five-year bands, which is the finest age detail ONS publishes at output area level.

measures.label: Dependency ratio
measures.note: Children under 15 plus residents 65 and over, per 100 residents aged 15 to 64. The standard demographic definition.

measures.label: Households with dependent children
measures.note: Married or civil partnership couples, cohabiting couples, lone parents and other household types, in each case with dependent children.

measures.label: Overcrowded households
measures.note: ONS's occupancy rating for bedrooms of −1 or less — the household has fewer bedrooms than the bedroom standard says it needs. The campaign page sets out the standard in full.

measures.label: Black, Black British, Caribbean or African
No passport held
measures.note: A real answer, not missing data. It tracks age and income as much as nationality.
measures.noteMissing: passports held was not asked in 2011

measures.label: English and/or British identity only
measures.note: Gives their national identity as English, British, or both, and nothing else. National identity is a multi-response question, so its categories do not sum to 100%.

measures.label: No religion
measures.note: Includes people who wrote in agnostic, atheist or humanist, which ONS classifies here at both censuses. Separate from the people who did not answer at all — that is its own measure.

measures.label: Jewish
measures.note: 1.7% of Londoners and heavily concentrated, so most of the map is empty until you find Barnet, Hackney or Harrow. The census records Jewish identity only here, not in the ethnic group question.

measures.label: Did not answer
measures.note: Religion is the only question on the census form nobody has to answer. This is not the same as having no religion, and it is not missing data — it is an answer in itself.

measures.label: Arrived since 2011
measures.note: Of just the residents born abroad, the percentage who arrived since 2011. Not the percentage of the whole population.
measures.noteMissing: year of arrival cannot be asked of a decade the census predates: the 2011 form's most recent band ends at 2011

measures.label: In the UK less than five years
measures.note: Of just the residents born abroad, the percentage who arrived in the five years before the census. Not the percentage of the whole population.

measures.label: Cannot speak English well
measures.note: Combines 'cannot speak English well' and 'cannot speak English'. The denominator is all residents aged 3 and over, matching ONS's own headline.

measures.label: No one speaks English as a main language
measures.noteMissing: household language was not published in 2011; only individual main language

measures.label: Some but not all adults speak English
measures.noteMissing: household language was not published in 2011; only individual main language

measures.label: Bad or very bad health
measures.note: Self-reported. STRONGLY confounded by age — a retirement suburb reports far more bad health than a student area for reasons that have nothing to do with the place. Use the age-adjusted measure to compare places.

measures.label: Bad health, age-adjusted
measures.note: Observed bad health against what this area's age profile predicts. London-wide age-specific rates are fitted from the output area data itself by non-negative least squares, and the ratio is shrunk toward 100 so that small areas, where a handful of cases would otherwise swing it wildly, are not over-read. Amber = worse health than its age mix predicts; blue = better.
measures.changeNote: On this view, a fall (amber) is an improvement, as it means there was less age-adjusted bad health in 2021 than 2011.

measures.label: Provides 20+ hours unpaid care a week
measures.note: People providing 20 or more hours of unpaid care a week.

measures.label: Unemployed
measures.note: Includes unemployed full-time students, who are counted separately by ONS.

measures.label: Retired
measures.noteMissing: 2011's 16-and-over table reports economically inactive as one total, without separating the retired

measures.label: Full-time students
measures.note: Economically active full-time students plus economically inactive students.

measures.label: Managerial and professional occupations
measures.note: Denominator is residents aged 16 and over who were in employment the week before the census — not all residents, which would draw the working-age map instead.

measures.label: Flats
measures.note: Purpose-built blocks, converted or shared houses, other converted buildings, and flats in commercial buildings.

domainMethod: population-weighted p2-p98 of the output-area distribution, shared by every area type and every census year
